docs.README_md.p0006:
ZAICODE is an operator workbench for running many AI coding agents at once over
many projects, without babysitting them. It is a modified build of
[ZCode]({protected0}) (desktop app, browser UI and agent
CLI) with a product layer on top: every project is driven by the
[SAIPEN]({protected1}) protocol, work is started, continued
and scheduled from one window, and the subscription CLIs you already pay for
(Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity) run as docked workers next to the in-app
agents.
docs.README_md.p0008:
**0.0.1** is the first tagged snapshot: a personal, Windows-first build that is
used daily.
docs.README_md.p0014:
That is all. Setup brings what the machine lacks (Git, Node.js, Python, as private
copies: no administrator rights), fetches ZAICODE, SAIPEN and SAIMAIL from GitHub,
builds the app on the machine and puts a ZAICODE shortcut on the desktop. The first
run takes 15-30 minutes; the window shows every step.
docs.README_md.p0016:
Free models work at once: ZAICODE starts its own router and fills the **SAIFREN**
pool from keyless free tiers, so a task typed into New task gets an answer with no
key, no account and no setting. Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity subscriptions are
optional and can be signed in any time.
docs.README_md.p0018:
**One whole, four parts.** The workspace (launcher, installer), the app, SAIPEN and
SAIMAIL are four repositories. Each updates on its own: *Settings -> ZAICODE ->
Updates* shows every part, updates it by hand or by itself (checked a few minutes
after the start and every six hours). A new app build is prepared while ZAICODE runs
and starts with the next start; your own edits in a clone are never overwritten.
From a terminal: {protected0}.
Autotroubleshoot: {protected1}. Details: [docs/ZAICODE_INSTALL.md](docs/ZAICODE_INSTALL.md).
docs.README_md.p0026:
- **Projects with a MAIN session.** Each project has one MAIN session (START,
  {protected0}) and helper sessions (subSaipens: WIKI, TEST, AUDIT, …). The
  default sidebar view shows the project row as its MAIN; ▶ continues MAIN
  instead of opening another session. CONTINUE ALL, DONE and CLEAR ALL DONE
  sweep every project; a session cut off mid-turn shows INTERRUPTED, never DONE.
- **Crash safety.** Sessions a dead process cut off and goals still active
  continue by themselves after a restart; running workers start again. Agents
  inside ZAICODE cannot kill ZAICODE by process name.
- **Workers.** Subscription CLIs run in terminals docked to any edge of the
  window (or in their own snapping windows). First-run "Trust this folder?"
  questions are answered; a worker that hits its usage limit is reported and,
  by setting, closed or restarted after the reset.
- **Limits and resets.** Quota meters per account and pool, a title-bar timer
  for the nearest reset with the full list of coming resets on hover.
- **SCHEDULER.** Prompts that start by themselves: at a time, daily, every N
  minutes or when a quota window refills; in one project or a whole sidebar
  section, worst projects (most blocked / open SAIPEN tickets) first. Conditions
  can stop stopgap work (free-pool sessions, weaker workers) first, run only on
  idle projects, or continue only marked sessions. Prompts have no practical
  length limit.
- **Routing.** A bundled 9router (MIT) gives zero-setup pools: SAIFREN
  (keyless free tiers) and SAIOPP (your subscriptions).
- **SAIHOME, timers, sounds, highlights.** An operator home with statistics,
  FastPrompter-style timers and alarms, per-action sounds and a Win95 dark
  golden, pixel-crisp interface.

docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0002:
ZAICODE is three projects that work as one: the ZAICODE app, SAIPEN (the
protocol that keeps agent work on track) and SAIMAIL (the mail agents use to
tell each other things). Installing them by hand means three clones, a Node.js
toolchain, a Python environment and a build. The installer does all of it:
run it, wait, and a ZAICODE shortcut is on the desktop.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0006:
- **[ZAICODE-Setup.exe]({protected0})**:
  download, double-click, press **INSTALL**. The window (gold on dark, the
  SAIPEN banner) shows every step as it runs, the time so far and the log on
  demand; at the end **START ZAICODE**, or **TRY AGAIN** / **Autotroubleshoot**
  / **Open log** when a step did not finish. Pointed at an existing ZAICODE
  folder the button reads **UPDATE**: the same run updates and repairs. The
  exe carries the install scripts and needs nothing next to it; it is built by
  {protected1} (the .NET Framework compiler every Windows 10/11
  has).
- {protected2} (double-click): the same install in a console.
- From nothing, in PowerShell:
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0010:
Setup options: {protected0} (preset folder),
{protected1} (starts at once), {protected2} (no window: the console installer, exit code
= result). The first run builds the app on this machine, which takes a while;
later runs only update and repair.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0012: ## Free models, nothing to set up
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0014:
The app ships its own 9router. On a machine without one ZAICODE runs it
privately (isolated mode, port 20138), fills **SAIFREN** from keyless free
tiers and makes {protected0} the model of new tasks, so the first task
typed into New task gets an answer: no key, no account, no setting. Claude
Code, Codex and Antigravity logins are optional; a login never set up on the
machine shows as "optional, sign in any time", not as a "needs you" item.
Proof: {protected1}
starts the packaged app on an empty profile (its own HOME, APPDATA and
LOCALAPPDATA) and passes only when the router is isolated, SAIFREN answers its
first-token probe and a task in New task is answered.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0018:
The workspace (launcher, installer), the app, SAIPEN and SAIMAIL are four
clones. Each one updates on its own: **Settings -> ZAICODE -> Updates** lists
them with their version and commit, updates one by hand or all of them, and
has a "by itself" switch per part (on by default in an installed ZAICODE, off
in a developer checkout). ZAICODE looks a few minutes after the start and then
every six hours. After an update each part gets what it needs: the app its
dependencies (when {protected0} moved) and a new build (staged while
ZAICODE runs, started on the next start), SAIPEN its launcher, SAIMAIL its
{protected1} install, the workspace a new root launcher. A clone on another branch,
with local commits, or with edits the update would overwrite is reported and
left exactly as it is.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0024:
The installer is the Autotroubleshoot checks run with "repair" on an empty
folder, in this order. Each step is idempotent, so running it again updates
the install and fixes what broke.

Every Claude Code or Codex login lives in its own home: {protected0},

docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0050:
{protected0}
checks a fresh install, seeds faults (shortcut and launcher deleted, SAIPEN
launcher pointed at a missing Python, SAIMAIL's venv deleted, node_modules
recorded for another lockfile, a leftover build folder deeper than MAX_PATH),
asserts the doctor reports and repairs every one, then starts the shortcut's
target with an isolated profile and stops exactly the process tree it started.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_INSTALL_md.p0052:
{protected0} builds four throw-away repositories on
disk and an install of their clones, then proves that a check changes nothing,
that one part updates alone with its follow-up (SAIPEN launcher, root
launcher), that overlapping local edits and local commits are kept, and that an
unknown part name is refused. No network.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0002:
How this checkout and a Claude Code Cloud session run one SAIPEN workspace
with different executor locality, and where the boundary between them is.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0008:
One branch carries the protocol state. There is no merge step, no rebase step
and no second local branch to keep in step: whichever executor has a verified
checkpoint commits and pushes it, and the other side takes it with a
fast-forward.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0010:
{protected0} is the pre-transport history and the published default branch. It is
not force-updated by the transport.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0012: ## What travels and what does not
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0014:
A checkpoint in this repository carries the SAIPEN protocol state, the root
launcher, the installer, the docs and these transport scripts. That is the
whole workspace layer.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0016:
It carries **no product byte**. {protected0} is a separate Git repository, listed
in {protected1} and gitignored at this root
({protected2}). Product work needs its own clone of {protected3} on branch
{protected4}, and that clone is a second, independent object with its own history.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0018:
The consequence is easy to get wrong: a clean {protected0} at this root says
nothing about uncommitted product work, and a {protected1} fast-forward says
nothing about product code. Check {protected2} explicitly.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0022:
Two scripts, both repo-owned so a new machine gets them from the repository
instead of from memory:
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0024:
| File | Role |
|------|------|
| {protected0} | validates, reconciles the branch, installs and starts the watcher, writes the autostart entry, proves local == remote |
| {protected1} | the loop: fetch, compare, fast-forward or push, log, pause; then the product pass and self-update |
| {protected2} | round-trip from an independent executor plus cold-recovery proof |
| {protected3} | product pass and self-update against throwaway Git repositories (no network, no real remote) |
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0030:
It is idempotent. Machine-local state lives in {protected0}:
{protected1} (a copy), {protected2} (rotated at
2 MB to {protected3}), {protected4} (single instance),
{protected5}, and a Startup-folder entry
{protected6}.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0032:
The installer refuses a dirty tree and never cleans it. If every dirty path is
canonical SAIPEN state under {protected0}, it says so and prints the exact
checkpoint commands; that is an uncheckpointed protocol state, not a transport
fault, and the installer will not commit it behind the protocol's back.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0036:
| Situation | Move |
|-----------|------|
| clean, local is an ancestor of remote | {protected0} |
| clean, remote is an ancestor of local | {protected1} |
| dirty | pause; not even a fetch |
| on another branch | pause |
| both advanced, no shared ancestor | pause, log both commit ids, merge nothing |
| fetch or network failed | log degraded, retry next tick |
| a merge/rebase{protected2} is in flight | pause |
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0038:
Never: force push, hard reset, stash, clean, checkout of a foreign branch,
commit, or a stop by process name. The installer stops a watcher only by the
pid it recorded in its own pid file.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0040:
A dirty tree costs nothing, because the watcher checks dirt before it fetches.
An idle checkout therefore makes no network calls at all.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0044:
{protected0} is its own repository, so the table above never moves product
code. After it, the same tick handles the product checkout ({protected1},
default {protected2}; branch {protected3}, default {protected4}). The
product pass runs whether or not the outer tree is dirty. It only ever pulls.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0046:
| Situation | Move |
|-----------|------|
| remote ahead, no incoming file is dirty here | {protected0}; uncommitted product work stays as it is |
| remote ahead, an incoming file is dirty here | HELD: log the files, merge nothing |
| local ahead | log; **never pushed** (product is published by SAIPEN SHIP) |
| diverged | pause, log both ids, merge nothing |
| other branch, a git op in flight, fetch failed | pause |
| no {protected1} checkout, or {protected2} | skipped |
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0048:
git refuses on its own a fast-forward that would overwrite a local change, so
the HELD check is an earlier, clearer guard, not the only one. A product
fast-forward does not rebuild anything: to test, run {protected0} (or
the dev preview).
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0052:
The watcher runs as a copy under {protected0}, so a newer watcher in
the repository never ran without a reinstall. In loop mode it now compares
its own file with the repository's committed copy on every pass. It installs
that copy over itself and restarts exactly once, with the same arguments,
only when all of these hold:
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0056:
A copy that does not parse is refused and logged, and the running watcher
carries on.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0058:
Watchers installed before T-90 lack both the product pass and self-update.
Re-run {protected0} once on such a machine; after that, the
watcher updates itself.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0062:
{protected0} at the root is the entry rule and
{protected1} is the execution procedure. The skill fetches
the SAIPEN kernel from {protected2} and runs it through the
declared engine surface {protected3}. The kernel is pinned by commit
({protected4}), never by tag. Tag {protected5} is an older kernel with the same
{protected6}; its {protected7} mutates state, and its validator rejects this board.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0064:
{protected0} records the kernel path of whichever executor checkpointed
last. In the cloud, the first {protected1} on kernel {protected2} converges
it to the running kernel as one journaled {protected3} (E-1410). On the operator
machine the pointer arrives dead in the same way. A kernel with automatic
convergence repairs it on {protected4}; otherwise run
{protected5}.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0066:
**The return trip is observed.** E-1562 (cloud) converged the pointer to
{protected0}; E-1571 (operator machine)
converged it straight back to {protected1}, automatically, with no manual
{protected2}. Both directions are the same automatic convergence, so expect
one {protected3} {protected4} per locality switch and treat it as expected noise
rather than a defect. It stays noise until P1-2
({protected5}) moves the pointer out of versioned
state; do not implement P1-2 as a side effect of noticing it. Never hand-edit
the pointer.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0068:
{protected0} may point at a kernel **development checkout** that is ahead
of the pin, not at a clean {protected1} clone — on the operator machine it is the
{protected2} branch with uncommitted work. A kernel that is not at the
pinned commit is not automatically wrong, but it is not a clean-room source
either, so the rule below about the voice contract applies to it with full
force. Never commit, stash, reset, check out or clean anything in such a
checkout; a targeted single-file restore of {protected3} is the only
permitted exception, and only when the operator asked for it.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0070: ### STYLE.md is not a local setting
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0072:
{protected0} must be **byte-identical to the pinned kernel's file** on
every machine, in every copy, with no exceptions and no local edits. There is
more than one copy on an operator machine:
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0074:
- the kernel checkout at {protected0} (a Git clone, on the operator
  machine a development checkout);
- {protected1}, populated by the
  {protected2} scheduled task ({protected3}). It is **not a
  Git repository**, so {protected4} can never repair it — a re-sync through
  the injector, or a direct write of the published content, is the only path.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0076:
The {protected0} token in {protected1} is a hash of that file's text
({protected2}, {protected3}: CRLF normalized, the
{protected4} line excluded). Edit {protected5} in one copy and the
token moves; the other copy and the cloud, which fetch the published kernel,
keep the published token, and every CLI write on the mismatching side is
refused with {protected6}.
That is the whole failure: the local side writes state the cloud cannot write.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0078:
**Changing the reply language is a kernel commit plus a repin**, never a local
edit. Change it in the kernel repository, publish it, re-pin the commit in
SKILL.md, and update {protected0} through {protected1}. A local
edit to {protected2} desynchronizes every machine that is not the one making it.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0080:
One trap worth naming: the published {protected0} is a machine-bound shim that
hardcodes one operator's absolute interpreter and checkout paths. It runs on
exactly one machine. The cloud must use {protected1}.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0082:
Shortcuts: {protected0} continues the current Work; {protected1} ingests the whole
message as source{protected2} and continues every eligible Work. Neither asks for
routine confirmation.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0086:
**AVAILABLE_IN_CLOUD** — protocol state and the workspace layer. Reading and
writing {protected0}, the launcher ({protected1}), the
installer under {protected2}, {protected3}, {protected4}, {protected5}, and the
transport scripts. Git read, commit, push and fetch on {protected6}. Any
gate that is a file assertion, a diff review or a text check.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0088: **LOCAL_WINDOWS_ONLY** — the gates that need this machine.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0090:
| Gate | Why |
|------|-----|
| {protected0} | compiles {protected1} with the .NET Framework {protected2}; no Windows SDK on a cloud image |
| packaged Electron E2E ({protected3} desktop, Solo → queue → dispatch) | needs a desktop session and a seeded provider profile |
| the live 9router | a Windows service on this machine |
| interactive desktop click-through | a human and a screen |
| the watcher's own runtime cases | the watcher only ever runs on the machine holding the checkout |
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0092:
These are recorded as local-only acceptance boundaries. They are never
reported as passed because the diff looked right.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0094:
**SAFE_TO_DEFER** — the product layer. A cloud session can clone
{protected0} branch {protected1} and work there. Workspace-layer work does
not require product work, but it does require the clone:
{protected2} declares {protected3}, and without it the
validator fails with {protected4}. {protected5} gates need the pinned pnpm 10.33.2
and a prepared workspace. {protected6} on a fresh cloud image is the
documented way in, and the product's {protected7} already declares it.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0096:
The cloud can verify only product bytes that are on {protected0}. A
product delta that exists only in the operator's {protected1} checkout is
invisible here, so every product gate for it is NOT RUN in the cloud, whatever
the gate. T-84 is the first case (E-1411): its fix was local-only while
{protected2} still carried the pre-fix code.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0098:
**UNSAFE_TO_EMULATE** — anything that would make a local-only gate look green.
Do not stub the launcher build, fake a packaged-app run, replay a recorded
{protected0} result as if it had just run, or convert "the code
looks correct" into a PASS line in {protected1}.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0100:
**KNOWN_CLOUD_DIVERGENCE** — conformance that depends on where the checkout
lives. On kernel {protected0} the cloud validator reports {protected1}
FAILs (T-47, T-62, T-76, T-78 at the time of writing) that the operator
machine does not.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0102:
The kernel moves any LOG event over 1024 bytes into a
{protected0} sidecar. On read it restores the sidecar only
when the checkout's absolute path equals the path it was written from. A long
VERIFY verdict written on Windows is therefore unreadable in the cloud, and the
reverse holds too.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0104:
The defect is in the kernel and is filed as P1-1 in
{protected0}. Until it lands:
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0108:
The same machine-path binding also blocks work. The pre-BUILD debt baseline
is captured the first time a ticket enters BUILD and re-checked on every later
entry. A ticket that first entered BUILD on the operator machine therefore
cannot enter BUILD in the cloud: the transition is refused with
{protected0}. T-84 is the case on record: DEBT-000079 was
captured at E-1377 and the transition refused at E-1446. Leave such a ticket to
the machine that captured its baseline.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0112:
If local and remote stop sharing an ancestor, the watcher stops. It does not
merge, rebase or force. Both commit ids go into the log, the fix is
{protected0} by hand, and
the result is checkpointed like any other change.
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0116: ### Environment setup script (one time, in the cloud environment's settings)
docs.docs_ZAICODE_SAIPEN_CLOUD_md.p0118:
Cloud environment menu in the session title bar -> Edit -> Setup script. It
